title: Jailer 2 Hindi Release On Track for October 15, Makers Deny Date Change
excerpt: After reports of a curtailed Hindi theatrical run, the Jailer 2 team says "there has been no change" — Pen Marudhar Entertainment will distribute in North India.
body:
• The Jailer 2 team has officially denied reports that the Hindi version's theatrical release was altered, confirming it will open in cinemas on Thursday, October 15, 2026, alongside the Tamil, Telugu and other language versions.
  • The speculation stemmed from reports of a four-week theatrical-to-OTT window for the Hindi version, versus the roughly eight-week window national multiplex chains like PVR INOX and Cinepolis typically hold for Hindi films.
  • Pen Marudhar Entertainment will distribute the Hindi version in North India, the makers confirmed.
  • Rajinikanth returns as "Tiger" Muthuvel Pandian in the Nelson Dilipkumar-directed sequel, with S. J. Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Vidya Balan and Ramya Krishnan co-starring.

The team behind Jailer 2 has issued an official clarification putting rumours to rest: the Rajinikanth-starrer's Hindi version will release in theatres on Thursday, October 15, 2026, as originally planned — and "there has been no change" to the schedule.

The statement addresses reports that the Hindi theatrical release had been altered or curtailed. "In light of recent media reports suggesting that Jailer 2 will not be releasing in Hindi, we would like to officially clarify that the film's Hindi version is scheduled for a theatrical release on Thursday, 15th October 2026, alongside its other language versions, as originally planned," the team said, according to Bollywood Hungama.

The makers also confirmed the North India distributor: "The film will be distributed in North India by Pen Marudhar Entertainment," and urged media outlets to "refrain from circulating any unverified information regarding the film's release."

Context & Background

The confusion began with reports linking the Hindi version to a four-week OTT window — the gap between theatrical release and streaming premiere — tied to a larger digital rights deal. Because national multiplex chains such as PVR INOX and Cinepolis generally observe an eight-week theatrical-to-OTT window for Hindi films, the shorter reported window fed speculation that the Hindi version might see a restricted theatrical presence, particularly in Hindi-speaking markets.

"Kerala presales reportedly crossed ₹1.61 crore in the first hour, with around 800 screens planned in the state."

The clarification is separate from the Kerala rollout already underway: Jailer 2 opens with 6 a.m. shows in Kerala on release day (bookings opened October 11), with Sree Gokulam Movies distributing there. Kerala presales reportedly crossed ₹1.61 crore in the first hour, with around 800 screens planned in the state.

Franchise Primer

Jailer 2 is the sequel to Jailer (2023), the Nelson Dilipkumar-directed action comedy that became one of Rajinikanth's strongest commercial successes in recent years. The first film cast Rajinikanth as retired jailer "Tiger" Muthuvel Pandian, a mild-mannered family man whose violent past resurfaces when his son goes missing — a setup that became a blockbuster through its dark comedy and a celebrated star-studded climax.

The sequel follows Tiger after his peaceful life is shattered by a syndicate seeking revenge for crime boss Varma's demise, forcing him undercover as a driver while protecting his family. Rajinikanth recently revealed at the film's pre-release event that he turned down sequel pitches for both Baashha and Petta — he is cautious about follow-ups that repeat a formula — before deciding Jailer's world had enough story left to justify a second chapter. He said revisiting the first film after its streaming release, and a warning from Varma about a larger network behind him, convinced him there was more to tell.

Cast & Crew

Rajinikanth headlines as "Tiger" Muthuvel Pandian, with S. J. Suryah as Bodhi Kalpak, Mithun Chakraborty as Kalpak, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Vidya Balan as Kantha Kalpak, Ramya Krishnan returning as Vijaya, Yogi Babu, Mirnaa, Jatin Sarna and Anna Rajan. Cameos include Mohanlal (Mathew), Shiva Rajkumar, Jackie Shroff, Vijay Sethupathi and Hrithik Roshan, with Nora Fatehi in an item number. Written and directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, produced by Kalanithi Maran under Sun Pictures, music by Anirudh Ravichander. Runtime is 165 minutes, certified U/A, releasing in Tamil, Telugu and Hindi in standard and IMAX formats.

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora, this is straightforward good news: the Hindi version will be available in theatres the same day as the original-language versions, so Hindi-speaking viewers — in the US, the Gulf and elsewhere — don't face a staggered rollout. If you're planning a first-weekend watch in the US, check your local theatre chain's listings in the days before October 15, as South Indian big-ticket releases often add screens based on advance demand.

What's Next

With the release locked for October 15, attention turns to advance booking numbers and first-day screen counts — and whether the film can convert its record Kerala presales into a pan-India opening. See also: Jailer 2 clears the censor board with a 165-minute runtime.

Sources: Bollywood Hungama, Pinkvilla
